item.description: Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest declined to the lowest level on record in the 12 months through July, according to data released by Brazilian space research agency Inpe on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu, Andre Romani
item.content:encoded: Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest declined to the lowest level on record in the 12 months through July, according to data released by Brazilian space research agency Inpe on Friday. Some 3,335 square kilometers (1,287.65 square miles) of Amazon jungle were destroyed in the 12 months through July, an all-time low in the historical series that goes back to 1988. It was a fall of about 42% from the preceding period. The previous lowest level for Brazil's Amazon deforestation was reached in 2011-2012, when 4,571 square kilometers were destroyed. In the mid-90s, the figure had reached a record high of nearly 30,000 square kilometers destroyed a year. The data released on Friday, which is produced yearly by Inpe's PRODES satellite monitoring program, is measured from August to July as there is less cloud cover in the middle of the year to obscure deforestation on satellite images. "The figures released today are a historic achievement," said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima, adding they show the world that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions." President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva took office in 2023 [USN:S0N37201F TEXT:"pledging to end deforestation"] by 2030, after it soared to its highest in 15 years during the administration of former President Jair Bolsonaro. Lula will face Bolsonaro's eldest son, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, in a [USN:S0N45N09L TEXT:"presidential election runoff"] on October 25, after the younger Bolsonaro performed better than expected in the first round. The senator pledged in his manifesto to strengthen environmental oversight in the Amazon, prioritizing areas under the greatest pressure from deforestation and wildfires. He said law enforcement would focus on organized crime rather than on extractive workers and small farmers. In Brazil's Cerrado savanna, deforestation fell about 24% in the period, to some 5,517 square kilometers, also the lowest on record in a series going back to 2001, Inpe data showed.

item.title: Producción de cobre en Perú cae 5,0% interanual en agosto, a 230.676 toneladas: gobierno
item.description: La producción de cobre de Perú, la tercera mayor a nivel mundial, cayó un 5,0% interanual en agosto, a unas 230.676 toneladas métricas, según un reporte del Ministerio de Energía y Minas difundido el viernes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La producción de cobre de Perú, la tercera mayor a nivel mundial, cayó un 5,0% interanual en agosto, a unas 230.676 toneladas métricas, según un reporte del Ministerio de Energía y Minas difundido el viernes. Entre enero y agosto la producción de cobre local aumentó un 1,2% interanual, a 1.829.790 toneladas métricas, detalló el ministerio en un informe preliminar sin más detalles. Perú produjo el año pasado unas 2,77 millones de toneladas de cobre, un nivel estable en los últimos tres años por la falta de nuevos proyectos, conflictos sociales y la disminución de las leyes del mineral en las grandes minas, según la industria.

item.title: US annual budget gap hits nearly $2 trillion, largest in 5 years
item.description: The US budget deficit rose by $217 billion to nearly $2 trillion in the 2026 fiscal year, fueled in part by tariff refunds and record spending to service the nation's more than $40 trillion in debt, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years, Treasury Department figures showed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Dan Burns
item.content:encoded: The US budget deficit rose by $217 billion to nearly $2 trillion in the 2026 fiscal year, fueled in part by tariff refunds and record spending to service the nation's more than $40 trillion in debt, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years, Treasury Department figures showed on Friday. Continued increases in spending for social benefits programs like Social Security and Medicare and a $48 billion jump in defense spending also factored into the increase. The $1.99 trillion deficit for the year ended September 30, the first full budget year of President Donald Trump's second term, was up from $1.78 trillion in fiscal 2025. It was the largest shortfall since fiscal 2021's $2.77 trillion budget gap, then fueled by COVID-19 pandemic relief spending, and is the third-largest annual deficit ever. Total receipts for fiscal 2026 were a record $5.40 trillion, up $169 billion, or 3%, from the $5.24 trillion in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 outlays also were a record at $7.40 trillion, up $386 billion, or 6%, from the $7.01 trillion in the prior fiscal year. Debt-service outlays totaled a record $1.36 trillion, climbing by $144 billion, or 12%, a spending category now eclipsed only by Social Security and the combined outlays for Medicare and Medicaid. Total US debt breached the $40 trillion milestone about two months ago. Another driver of the widening shortfall was a $22 billion drop in net tariff receipts following a Supreme Court ruling this year negating a large portion of the tariffs Trump had imposed during his first year in office. That triggered $145 billion of tariff refunds over this year, resulting in an 11% decline in net tariff income to about $173 billion. Defense spending for the year rose by 6% to $917 billion. A US Treasury official said it was not clear how much of the increase could be attributed to the war Trump and Israel started against Iran earlier this year. The Treasury official said the department calculated an estimated deficit-to-GDP ratio of 6.2% for fiscal 2026, but declined to say what GDP estimate was used. This figure compares to an actual 5.8% deficit-to-GDP ratio for fiscal 2025. For the 2026 fiscal year's final month of September, the Treasury reported a deficit of $27 billion versus a $198 billion surplus a year earlier.

item.title: Canada exploring Stelco nationalization, industry minister says
item.description: Canada is exploring all options under the Investment Canada Act to consider nationalizing steel maker Stelco, owned by US-listed Cleveland Cliffs , Industry Minister Melanie Joly said on Friday in Toronto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada is exploring all options under the Investment Canada Act to consider nationalizing steel maker Stelco, owned by US-listed Cleveland Cliffs (CLF.N) , Industry Minister Melanie Joly said on Friday in Toronto. "We believe there has been multiple breaches of commitments (by Cleveland Cliffs) and section 40 of the ICA offers options through a court process to make sure the company obliges to the commitment made," Joly said

item.title: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) to start vs. Bears
item.description: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. did not receive an injury designation on Friday and is on track to start Sunday's game against the visiting Chicago Bears.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. did not receive an injury designation on Friday and is on track to start Sunday's game against the visiting Chicago Bears. Penix, who has been a full participant in practice this week, sustained a rib injury late in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Tua Tagovailoa replaced Penix in overtime and threw a game-ending interception on his second play. Penix, 26, missed the first two weeks of this season to complete his recovery from ACL surgery. He has completed 67.5% of his passes for 719 yards, three touchdowns and one interception while posting a 2-1 record in three starts. Atlanta defensive end Za'Darius Smith (neck) has cleared the concussion protocol but is listed as questionable to play on Sunday. Cornerback C.J. Henderson (groin) has been ruled out for the Falcons (2-3). --Field Level Media

item.title: Ravens rule out QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) vs. Browns
item.description: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury on Sunday at Cleveland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury on Sunday at Cleveland. Tyler Huntley will start under center when the Ravens (4-1) visit the AFC North rival Browns (3-2), the team confirmed Friday. Jackson has not practiced since sustaining the injury late in the first half in the Week 4 win against the Tennessee Titans. Earlier this week, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said the two-time NFL MVP remains "definitely day-to-day." "To Lamar's credit, he's working his butt off," Minter said Wednesday. "He's doing everything he can to be out here. And when he's able to be, he will." Jackson, 29, has completed 70.8% of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception in four games this season. He has rushed for 144 yards and one score. Huntley, 28, completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in last Sunday's 30-23 overtime win at Atlanta. His 1-yard touchdown run in overtime gave Baltimore its third straight win. --Field Level Media

item.title: Putin concorda em cooperar com apelo do papa Leão por ajuda a cidade ucraniana
item.description: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, disse ao papa Leão que havia concordado em cooperar depois que o pontífice lhe pediu, nesta sexta-feira, que ajude a levar suprimentos essenciais para a cidade ucraniana de Oleshky, controlada pela Rússia, informou o Kremlin.
item.dc:creator: Joshua McElwee
item.content:encoded: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, disse ao papa Leão que havia concordado em cooperar depois que o pontífice lhe pediu, nesta sexta-feira, que ajude a levar suprimentos essenciais para a cidade ucraniana de Oleshky, controlada pela Rússia, informou o Kremlin. Leão ligou para Putin e pediu que ele providenciasse um cessar-fogo para permitir a entrada de ajuda humanitária e alimentos na cidade, tomada pelas forças russas em fevereiro de 2022, informou o Vaticano. Moradores relataram um agravamento da crise alimentar. Leão expressou “profunda preocupação” com a situação humanitária no local, acrescentou o Vaticano. Rússia e Ucrânia acusam-se mutuamente de bloquear o envio de suprimentos para a cidade, que as forças ucranianas pretendem retomar. “A intenção do Vaticano de ajudar a criar as condições necessárias para garantir a segurança da população da cidade e organizar o fornecimento de suprimentos essenciais recebeu apoio”, afirmou o Kremlin em comunicado. O comunicado não mencionou um cessar-fogo. “Ficou acordado que haverá cooperação nessa questão”, acrescentou. Sabe-se que Leão e Putin já haviam conversado uma vez anteriormente, em junho de 2025. O papa também reafirmou o compromisso da Santa Sé com quaisquer iniciativas em prol da paz, informou o Vaticano. O papa, de 71 anos, está se recuperando no hospital Gemelli, em Roma, após uma cirurgia para retirada de um câncer de pulmão. O Vaticano informou na manhã desta sexta-feira que ele apresenta melhora constante e está apto a trabalhar e realizar atividades diárias normais. O Kremlin informou que Putin desejou a Leão uma recuperação rápida e completa. O secretário de Estado do Vaticano, cardeal Pietro Parolin, disse aos repórteres após a ligação que a iniciativa partiu de Leão. O papa, segundo ele, queria “defender a causa dessa cidade sitiada”. A Rússia reconheceu problemas graves com alimentos e suprimentos médicos em Oleshky e afirmou que suas Forças Armadas estavam trabalhando para resolvê-los. O país culpou a Ucrânia pela crise, alegando que ela estava impedindo que esses suprimentos chegassem à cidade. A Ucrânia afirmou que é a Rússia quem está impedindo as entregas de alimentos. Oleshky, na região de Kherson, na Ucrânia, tinha uma população de cerca de 24 mil habitantes antes da guerra e ainda abriga cerca de 1.700 residentes, incluindo 47 crianças, segundo Danielle Bell, chefe da Missão de Monitoramento dos Direitos Humanos da ONU na Ucrânia.

item.title: EU to propose import curbs on other Chinese sectors, says EU chief
item.description: The European Commission will propose curbs on imports from China going beyond the safeguard measures it agreed with Beijing to halve inbound shipments of Chinese hybrid cars, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Philip Blenkinsop
item.content:encoded: The European Commission will propose curbs on imports from China going beyond the safeguard measures it [USN:L6N45V0LF TEXT:"agreed with Beijing"] to halve inbound shipments of Chinese hybrid cars, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Friday. Von der Leyen told a news conference after an EU summit that the deal struck with China would not fix the structural imbalance. The EU's goods trade deficit with China is running at more than €1 billion ($1.12 billion) a day. "And this is why we need to act," she said. "Our industries have called for action and we have heard them and we will respond, including some more safeguards." She said this was clearly supported by EU leaders. French President Emmanuel Macron told reporters after the summit that the EU should focus on measures for chemicals, plastics and ferro-alloys. Von der Leyen said that she welcomed a [USN:L6N45R0Q0 TEXT:"Franco-German paper"] published last month, which proposed the European Union reinforce its economy by enacting a new rapid-action measure to strike back against countries that harm it. She said the Commission would develop a new instrument to rapidly limit access to the EU single market where this was in the bloc's interest. She also said the EU's executive Commission would make a proposal in December for a new instrument that would limit EU companies' reliance on single sources for certain critical supplies. The Commission would also propose a "solidarity mechanism" to help countries or sectors that are subject to coercion or retaliation from outside the EU. ($1 = 0.8913 euros)

item.title: Uncertain forecast affects ALCS Game 4 plans for Guardians, Rays
item.description: CLEVELAND -- The Guardians have wrested home-field advantage from the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Championship Series and taken a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven matchup.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: CLEVELAND -- The Guardians have wrested home-field advantage from the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Championship Series and taken a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven matchup. Beyond that, little is certain as the teams prepare to play Game 4 on Friday night. Guardians manager Stephen Vogt and Rays counterpart Kevin Cash initially did not name their starting pitchers, despite inquiries on the subject. Extended periods of rain are also in the forecast, forcing MLB officials to work on contingency plans if a postponement occurs. The next two games take place in Cleveland before Sunday's scheduled travel day. "Having as much momentum as we can possibly have and being able to feed off of that, it's a lot of fun," said Guardians center fielder Petey Halpin, who hit his first postseason home run on Thursday in Game 3. "We feed off the crowd, feed off the energy. It's great." Halpin's two-run homer in the fifth inning gave Cleveland the lead for good in a 3-2 victory. It continued a breakout postseason for the 24-year-old rookie, who is batting .364 (4-for-11) with an .818 slugging percentage since moving into the lineup for the Guardians' win-or-go-home Game 5 against the Chicago White Sox on Saturday night. In one of the most improbable scenes in recent memory, Halpin unleashed a 25-foot-high bat flip after taking Griffin Jax deep Thursday -- and basked in chants of "Pe-tey" each time he came to the plate or fielded a ball the rest of the afternoon. "The bat flip was maybe a little much, if you ask me, but the moment was so exciting," said Guardians closer Cade Smith. "We're thrilled when stuff like that happens. It's so much fun. Guys are jumping around, giving high-fives, so it's a lot of fun." Cleveland's pitching plan has come together well for potential Games 6 and 7 on the road, which would see Parker Messick and postseason strikeout leader Gavin Williams go on normal rest. The Guardians will turn to right-hander Shawn Armstrong (0-0, 0.00) to start Game 4 as an opener. Armstrong allowed one hit over 1 2/3 scoreless innings in a no-decision against Tampa Bay on Tuesday. He was not as fortunate in his previous encounter with the Rays, permitting three runs on one hit in two-thirds of an inning in a no-decision on July 24 in an 11-3 loss. Armstrong, 36, has a 6.92 ERA without a decision in 15 career relief appearances versus the Rays. Tampa Bay is one of eight teams Armstrong has played for during his 12-season career. Tampa Bay, which won Game 2 at home, will hand the start to Nick Martinez on Friday. The 36-year-old right-hander pitched 3 2/3 innings and gave up two runs against the New York Yankees when he started Game 3 of the ALDS on Oct. 7. Martinez went 15-6 with a 3.10 ERA in the regular season over 31 starts, but Cash made him a bullpen option earlier in the ALCS. "The first game, I sat in the bullpen and didn't really like it," Martinez said, chuckling. "I was in the dugout with cleats on the second game. Whatever the team needs, I'm up for it. That's got to be my mentality for the rest of the year." Martinez pitched brilliantly against the Guardians during the regular season. He won both of his starts while permitting just seven hits and one walk over 13 scoreless innings. He added nine strikeouts as Cleveland's batters posted a .159/.178/.182 slash line against him. "We're just going to take it as we go, right?" Martinez said. "Not much you can control about that, so just be ready to go." Martinez is 3-2 with a 4.39 ERA in eight career appearances (four starts) versus Cleveland. --Brian Dulik, Field Level Media

item.title: Angola's fuel subsidies spending projected to hit $4 billion in 2026, official says
item.description: Angola could spend up to 3.8 trillion kwanzas ($4.16 billion) on fuel subsidies this year, nearly double its initial projections of less than 2 trillion kwanzas, a senior finance official told Reuters on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Rae Wee
item.content:encoded: Angola could spend up to 3.8 trillion kwanzas ($4.16 billion) on fuel subsidies this year, nearly double its initial projections of less than 2 trillion kwanzas, a senior finance official told Reuters on Friday. The increase underscores the fiscal strain facing the oil-producing nation, as surging energy prices from the ongoing war in the Middle East drive up the cost of keeping domestic fuel prices low. The mounting bill is adding pressure on the government to accelerate its gradual removal of subsidies, which began in 2023, but authorities are wary of moving too quickly for fear of economic and social fallout, Ottoniel dos Santos, Angola's secretary of state for finance and the treasury, told Reuters. "We need to move not only with the subsidies removal, but also with the diversification of our economy," said dos Santos in an interview on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok. "For now, it's been taken as it is - slowly," he added, referring to the scaling back of subsidies. "But if there is any window that could be used... and if we expect the impact on those who are more vulnerable are less than we forecast, then it will be easy to implement." The country now expects oil prices to average around $90 per barrel by the end of the year, higher than the reference price of $61 it used in its 2026 budget. Although the government has yet to submit its 2027 budget, due at the end of the month, dos Santos said its oil price assumption would not differ significantly from the International Monetary Fund's forecast of $71.50 a barrel. The government expects crude production to come in at 1.045 million barrels per day in 2027, matching this year's output. DIVERSIFYING FUNDING NEEDS Angola's $4 billion Eurobond issuance and other liability operations have covered the "majority" of the country's funding needs this year, dos Santos said, with any plans for further bond issuances or external financing dependent on the 2027 budget. "This is something that we will have to see what will be the needs for 2027 and identify if there is an opportunity or not for us to come back to the market," he told Reuters, adding that the country is [USN:L8N4510C2 TEXT:"actively opening up"] its domestic government bond market to foreign investors. The government is welcoming "all investors, all the regions" to buy Angolan debt, and is stepping up efforts to educate investors on access to its capital market. "Some investors think that the capital account is still closed, that it'll be difficult to get out when they get in, but actually it's not happening," said dos Santos. "We want to go everywhere, we want them to come as well... we want people to know that Angola is opening the domestic market to get opportunities from other investors, from other countries." ($1 = 913.0000 kwanzas)

Its selloff, though, has greater significance for markets than its size implies.The slump in the shares and bonds of the $39 bi

Analysis:Why CoreWeave is in the crosshairs of the AI scare

Michael Intrator, Chief Executive Officer of CoreWeave Inc., attends an interview with CNBC on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, U.S., September 22, 2025. REUTERS/Jeenah Moon/File Photo

FAST

LONDON/BENGALURU, Oct 16 : Loss-making and deeply indebted US cloud company CoreWeave became an easy target this week for investors concerned about an artificial intelligence bubble. Its selloff, though, has greater significance for markets than its size implies. The slump in the shares and bonds of the $39 billion Nvidia-backed AI infrastructure company came after third-quarter reports from hyperscalers hinted at delays in data center projects and a slower pace of growth in capital expenditure. Worried investors took aim at new-age AI-based cloud firms, or neoclouds, such as CoreWeave, conceivably the weakest links in the AI ecosystem because of how they borrow heavily to finance chips, land and energy for data centers which will yield income only in the future. CoreWeave's shares dived more than 15 per cent this week while yields on its 2030 bonds jumped 500 basis points to near 16 per cent.

CoreWeave chief Mike Intrator told employees in a memo, seen by Reuters, markets can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally" and it has a strong pipeline of demand. The company did not respond to Reuters' requests for comment. Investors focused instead on its $50 billion debt and the perils of being trapped in the middle of a circular financing arrangement between chipmakers such as Nvidia and clients such as Meta Platforms and OpenAI. "The problem with this stuff is that we're talking about huge interconnectedness, not just circular financing but the fact that these assets are all held in the same places, in the same portfolios, by the same types of investors," said James Athey, fixed-income portfolio manager at Marlborough. "And leverage is always that thing which turns a storm into a teacup into something more nefarious," he said, referring broadly to the AI jitters. Companies such as CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital, Iren, Lambda Labs, Crusoe and TeraWulf are building energy-intensive data centers they can eventually rent out to firms developing and running AI models. That calls for massive upfront investment and very little income until the leases begin. CoreWeave has never turned a profit, according to data compiled by LSEG. CoreWeave's CEO also said in the memo that its deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations. The company had a $104.2 billion revenue backlog at the end of the second quarter, followed by more than $25 billion in new commitments early in the third quarter. But the New Jersey-based company is burning cash faster than investors like. In 2025, CoreWeave reported annual revenue of $5.1 billion and a net loss of $1.2 billion. While revenue is expected to double this year, capital expenditure is estimated to be up fourfold to between $35 billion and $39 billion, leading to even more cash burn this year. News that Intrator and entities linked to him have sold nearly $1 billion of stock since the company's IPO in March last year, mostly under prearranged trading plans as per regulatory filings, has not helped. "Clearly they will need a capital injection or a bailout. They are burning capital, and capital is no longer free," said Alberto Gallo, founder of hedge fund Andromeda Capital. "You want to buy debt in businesses that have visible cash flow, typically as a bond investor, not someone that is doing capex, in the hope that there will be more capex needed in the future," he said. The firm holds bets against CoreWeave bonds. DOUBTS APLENTY CoreWeave is at the top of the 100-odd neoclouds that research firm Gartner Inc says are "the most exposed to the imbalance between revenue and capital spending" and need to soon earn returns to sustain operations. Gartner expects that by 2030, 80 per cent of neocloud providers will cease independent operations. "We are in a situation in which there are a lot of expectations on revenues and revenue growth, but this revenue growth is being fueled by the wrong type of capital, which is debt, not equity," said Tommaso Leodari, Dubai-based chief investment officer of hedge fund Index & Cie. The fund does not hold stakes in pure AI firms. "In the specific case of CoreWeave, these guys are financing their entire business with debt. So if anything happens in the utilization of this particular asset or if there is a slowing down on the construction of these data centers, it will reflect in problems in repaying the debt." A streak of warnings from AI hyperscalers such as Microsoft and Oracle Corp on delays in data center projects, power and component bottlenecks, a glut in high-end chips, alongside plans by giants such as Meta and Microsoft to launch their own chips to rival Nvidia's, have also stoked concerns about neoclouds. The pace at which revenue is growing at AI giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic, while still fast, has also softened. "Even at $10 billion revenue, CoreWeave is losing $2.5 billion, so there are no scale effects in the industry clear as yet," wrote Michael Frazis of Sydney-based Frazis Capital Partners. CoreWeave has Nvidia's backing. The chip giant has agreed to buy unsold CoreWeave compute capacity through April 2032, guaranteeing it will have a buyer for capacity not sold to customers. Ratings agencies have CoreWeave's debt marked as speculative grade, yet Sean Cray, vice president at Moody’s Ratings, pointed out the company does not speculatively purchase chips and has multiple avenues for financing. Originally a bitcoin miner, CoreWeave has still been an easy mark for punters, and hedge funds have been buying its junk-rated bonds for the high yield. The cost of insuring its debt against default climbed to about 1,200 basis points this week, signalling severe distress. "CoreWeave's credit selloff risks becoming a self-fulfilling prophecy," wrote Saurav Sen at research firm Gimme Credit. "The concern is less whether customers want the capacity than whether CoreWeave can afford to deliver it."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Bucks move start time for home opener, avoid World Series conflict
item.description: The NBA moved up the tipoff of the Bucks' home opener against the Chicago Bulls on Oct. 23 to avoid a conflict with Game 1 of the World Series, which will be held in Milwaukee that evening.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The NBA moved up the tipoff of the Bucks' home opener against the Chicago Bulls on Oct. 23 to avoid a conflict with Game 1 of the World Series, which will be held in Milwaukee that evening. Per the Bucks, their home opener was moved to 3 p.m. CT. The original start time for the game was 7 p.m., the same as the first pitch of Game 1 of the Fall Classic. The Milwaukee Brewers punched their ticket to the World Series on Thursday by completing a four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. The Brewers will face either the Tampa Bay Rays or Cleveland Guardians. The Guardians lead 2-1 in the American League best-of-seven series. "The Brewers' return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years is a special moment for Milwaukee and sports fans across Wisconsin," the Bucks said in a statement. "Congratulations to the Brewers and the entire organization on this tremendous achievement, and we'll be cheering them on as they begin their World Series run." --Field Level Media

item.title: Irish public sector trade unions suspend second day of strikes
item.description: Irish public sector trade unions suspended a second day of widespread strikes planned for next week after they agreed on Friday to begin mediated discussions with the government this weekend on the terms for new pay talks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Irish public sector trade unions suspended a second day of widespread strikes planned for next week after they agreed on Friday to begin mediated discussions with the government this weekend on the terms for new pay talks. Much of Ireland's public sector including teachers, health workers and civil servants on Wednesday staged the country's [USN:L1N4600B0 TEXT:"first major strike"] in almost two decades after failing for months to agree with ministers on the basis for negotiations on pay rises. The two sides agreed on Friday to begin a process aimed at finding a basis for formal negotiations to commence. "I believe that there is now a prospect of progress in the process that has been established. Obviously we will need to see the government's words backed up in practice," Kevin Callinan, chair of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions public services committee, told national broadcaster RTE.

item.title: Novartis ends mid-stage Fabhalta trial targeting serious kidney condition
item.description: Swiss drugmaker Novartis has terminated a mid-stage study testing its drug Fabhalta in patients with a serious kidney condition, citing "strategic considerations", according to a federal clinical trials registry.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Swiss drugmaker Novartis (NOVN.S) has terminated a mid-stage study testing its drug Fabhalta in patients with a serious kidney condition, citing "strategic considerations", according to a federal clinical trials registry. The trial was evaluating whether the oral medication was safe and effective for treating lupus nephritis when added to standard medical care Lupus nephritis is a severe inflammation of the kidneys caused by the autoimmune disease lupus The government database, last updated on October 15, shows Novartis decided to conclude the study after completing the first part It gives no other explanation and does not say whether safety or effectiveness played a role Endpoints News reported the development earlier on Friday Novartis did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment The US FDA first approved Fabhalta in 2023 for a rare blood disorder called PNH. It has since been approved for two kidney diseases, IgA nephropathy and C3 glomerulopathy

item.title: Enviado de Putin diz que Rússia e EUA discutem acordos conjuntos, incluindo data centres
item.description: Rússia e EUA estão discutindo uma série de novos projetos conjuntos, incluindo data centres movidos a energia nuclear, na esteira do acordo sobre diesel firmado na semana passada, disse nesta sexta-feira o enviado para investimentos do presidente Vladimir Putin.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Soldatkin, Olesya Astakhova
item.content:encoded: Rússia e EUA estão discutindo uma série de novos projetos conjuntos, incluindo data centres movidos a energia nuclear, na esteira do acordo sobre diesel firmado na semana passada, disse nesta sexta-feira o enviado para investimentos do presidente Vladimir Putin. Kirill Dmitriev afirmou que as sanções dos EUA representam sérios obstáculos e criticou como “equivocada” a Lei Graham, assinada pelo presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, no mês passado, que visa reduzir as receitas energéticas da Rússia por meio de sanções e tarifas. No entanto, ele disse que os dois países estão considerando outras formas de cooperação econômica na esteira do acordo sobre o diesel. “Também estamos discutindo projetos conjuntos na área de data centres russos e norte-americanos, inclusive com o uso de usinas nucleares de pequena escala”, acrescentou ele, sem dar detalhes. Neste mês, a Ucrânia atacou centros de dados do grupo de tecnologia russo Yandex e do grupo bancário e tecnológico Sberbank, no que classificou como uma resposta a ataques russos contra instalações ucranianas. Dmitriev, figura-chave nas negociações entre a Rússia e os EUA para pôr fim à guerra na Ucrânia, vem há muito tempo pressionando por uma série de acordos potenciais ambiciosos, inclusive sobre minerais e energia. O Kremlin tem manifestado frustração pelo fato de os EUA, até agora, terem vinculado tais acordos a um acordo de paz, que continua indefinido. Mas Dmitriev demonstrou otimismo de que isso está mudando. “Naturalmente, o progresso é bastante difícil; há resistência — resistência generalizada, na verdade — de vários setores. No entanto, como demonstra o exemplo do diesel, acredito que em breve anunciaremos várias outras iniciativas significativas. O gelo, de fato, começou a se quebrar”, disse ele na conferência Russian Energy Week, em Moscou. “Estamos efetivamente implementando projetos com os Estados Unidos da América neste exato momento e continuaremos a fazê-lo até que a operação militar especial chegue ao fim”, acrescentou ele, usando o termo do Kremlin para se referir à guerra. Dmitriev disse que o Tesouro dos EUA havia solicitado ao fundo soberano da Rússia, que ele dirige, que ajudasse a resolver questões complexas de pagamento relacionadas ao acordo sobre o diesel. O acordo anunciado por Trump há uma semana envolve o fornecimento de diesel russo aos mercados dos EUA e globais, a fim de reduzir o preço do combustível — uma prioridade para o presidente dos EUA antes das eleições de meio de mandato do próximo mês.

item.title: Swiss finance minister warns steep European debt could trigger euro crisis
item.description: Rising public debt levels in Europe and beyond pose a risk to economic stability and could trigger a euro crisis, Swiss Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rising public debt levels in Europe and beyond pose a risk to economic stability and could trigger a euro crisis, Swiss Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter said on Friday. Speaking to Swiss national broadcaster SRF in Bangkok on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, Keller-Sutter said energy prices were also fuelling concerns among policymakers. Switzerland has one of the lowest levels of public debt in Europe, but Keller-Sutter said it was important to see the bigger picture in the current environment. "We're so deeply interconnected internationally that we're also vulnerable, for instance, in case a debt crisis arises due to the sovereign debt of major countries. "I'm thinking in particular of the United States, but also of Europe; we have France - that could lead to a euro crisis," Keller-Sutter told SRF. France's public debt, budget deficits and tepid economic growth have [USN:L6N45Y0KA TEXT:"fed concern"] about its finances as political fragmentation has complicated fiscal consolidation efforts.

item.title: Indian police detain 'cockroach' founder, student leaders ahead of Delhi rally
item.description: Indian police detained protest leader Abhijeet Dipke and several protesters demanding the election chief's resignation over the removal of more than 130 million voters from the voter lists.
item.dc:creator: CNA

Indian police detain 'cockroach' founder, student leaders ahead of Delhi rally

Indian police detained protest leader Abhijeet Dipke and several protesters demanding the election chief's resignation over the removal of more than 130 million voters from the voter lists.

Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and Neha Bora, national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA) gesture as they addresses a press conference in New Delhi, India, Oct 15, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Adnan Abidi)

FAST

NEW DELHI: Police detain ed India's 'cockroach' movement founder Abhijeet Dipke, student leaders and supporters on Friday (Oct 16) as hundreds poured into central Delhi, waving the national flag and demand ing the resignation of India's election chief. The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), opposition groups and student organisations have held near- daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists th ey say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision . T he Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. Dipke called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders detain ed and sent to jail this week for five days for demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban.

The group and left-wing student organisations had urged supporters to gather at the Central Park in New Delhi 's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag.

Protestors amid security personnels chant slogans as they take part in a flag rally by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, Oct 16, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Bhawika Chhabra)

POLICE SAY THEY WARNED MOVEMENT LEADER AGAINST PROTESTING Dipke was detain ed as he stepped out of a house in central Delhi , with police hauling him into a police car and driving away after a brief argument. Student activist Neha Bora, a prominent face of the protests, was also detain ed as she tried to reach Connaught Place with dozens of supporters. Senior police officer Sachin Sharma told Reuters that Dipke and Bora had been taken into preventive detention. "Abhijeet is detain ed by Delhi Police ," CJP posted on X. "This government is so scared of the youth waving national flag." Earlier on Friday, police had met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest. Security was stepped up , w ith hundreds of police in riot gear fanning out across central Delhi. The park was shut by civic authorities. Nevertheless, nearly 500 protesters managed to reach Connaught Place in groups and protested in about half a dozen places around the Central Park, waving flags and shouting slogans. A few were detained and taken away in a police vehicle. "If waving the tricolour in the country has become a crime then I am happy to go to jail," said Saurav Kumar, a data analyst, before he was detained. "The government not giving us the space to protest, not accepting faults in the system is not a healthy sign for a democracy." Small protests were also held in financial capital Mumbai and tech hub Bengaluru, while student organisations held a demonstration in the eastern city of Patna, with people waving flags of their organisations and pushing against police barricades.

Protestors chant slogans as they take part in a flag rally by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India, Oct 16, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Bhawika Chhabra)

YOUTH USED AS PAWNS, BJP SAYS The cockroach movement has emerged as one of the biggest political challenges faced by Modi and his BJP in his 12 years in power. A weeks-long sit-in by its supporters earlier this year forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over exam paper leaks. The latest demonstrations erupted after the Indian Express newspaper reported that Kumar's two deputies had raised concerns internally about voter list changes, registration procedures and digital systems. The 130 million names that were removed from voter lists starting last year - equivalent to more than the population of Japan - included 28 million people who had died, 63 million who relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced, according to the Election Commission. Opposition parties allege the deletions disproportionately affect Muslims and other minorities who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, allegations the commission and the BJP reject. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said the demonstrations were the main opposition Congress party's attempt to "seize power". "Instead of channelling the energy of the youth toward nation-building, they are being used as pawns in the politics of anarchy," he said at a media briefing on Friday.

Related:

Security stepped up in India's capital for 'cockroach' movement rally

Across the border, India’s ‘cockroach’ movement draws young Pakistani interest

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Trump says neither he nor Musk responsible for Ukraine loss of Starlink access
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he did not think either he or Elon Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access in a way that affected its military operations against Russia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he did not think either he or Elon Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access in a way that affected its military operations against Russia. The reduction in services provided by the satellite company interrupted communications with headquarters and caused internet speeds to drop. Reuters reported on Thursday that the White House approved the [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"reduction in Starshield services"]. Trump, speaking to reporters as he left the White House on a trip to Georgia, said neither he nor Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access. Any limit to Ukraine's access to the Starshield system was not imposed by the United States, Trump added. Starshield was developed by SpaceX specifically for government and national-security customers, particularly the US Department of Defense. Starshield uses the Starlink constellation as its backbone. Trump also he has a good relationship with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.

item.title: Division II DB Tyler Ulrich dies days after in-game injury
item.description: A North Texas community and an Oklahoma college campus are in mourning following the death of defensive back Tyler Ulrich, who died five days after suffering a traumatic injury in a game.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A North Texas community and an Oklahoma college campus are in mourning following the death of defensive back Tyler Ulrich, who died five days after suffering a traumatic injury in a game. Ulrich, from Azle, Texas, was injured in the game between his team, Southern Nazarene, and Ouachita Baptist in Arkadelphia, Ark., last Saturday in an NCAA Division II meeting. The school announced the passing of the sophomore finance major on Thursday. "When I think of good, I think of Tyler Ulrich," Jason Vines, who coached him at Azle High School, told WFAA. "One of the sweetest young men I've ever been around, ever known." Southern Nazarene, based in Bethany, Okla., canceled its game set for this Saturday at Southwestern Oklahoma State. After the 49-14 loss at Ouachita, the university confirmed Ulrich, 21, was in critical condition but never specified the injury. In a statement issued Thursday, Southern Nazarene asked the community to keep Ulrich's family in their thoughts. "This loss is deeply felt across our campus," read a school statement posted to X. "Our hearts are with his family, friends, teammates, and everyone who knew him. We ask that you join us in lifting them up in prayer." In six games for Southern Nazarene this season, Ulrich made 39 tackles. He was in his third season with the Crimson Storm. --Field Level Media

item.title: Djokovic returns to Basel for first time since 2011 in ATP Finals bid
item.description: Novak Djokovic on Friday received a wildcard entry into the Swiss Indoors Basel, setting up his first appearance at the tournament since 2011 as the 24-times Grand Slam champion pursues a place at the ATP Finals and the 103rd title of his career.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Novak Djokovic on Friday received a wildcard entry into the Swiss Indoors Basel, setting up his first appearance at the tournament since 2011 as the 24-times Grand Slam champion pursues a place at the ATP Finals and the 103rd title of his career. The 39-year-old Serbian arrives in Switzerland after a mixed Asian swing, where he captured a [USN:L6N45S0UI TEXT:"record seventh China Open crown"] before suffering a [USN:L1N45V0DT TEXT:"surprise second-round defeat"] by Poland's Hubert Hurkacz at the Shanghai Masters, a tournament he has won a record four times. Djokovic has endured an uneven season by his lofty standards. The former world number one [USN:L4N44R04U TEXT:"exited the US Open"] in the first round, his earliest Grand Slam defeat since the 2006 Australian Open. The decision to add Basel to his schedule comes as something of a surprise after Djokovic said following his early exit in Shanghai that he planned to play only the Paris Masters, scheduled for November 2-8, before the season-ending ATP Finals. Basel offers Djokovic an opportunity to strengthen his bid for a 17th ATP Finals appearance. He sits 11th in the ATP Live Race to Turin and needs to finish inside the top nine, with world number one [USN:L1N45S0CV TEXT:"Jannik Sinner sidelined"] for the remainder of 2026 because of a persistent knee injury. Djokovic will make his fourth appearance in Basel, having lifted the trophy in 2009 by beating Swiss great Roger Federer in the final. He joins a strong field that includes Canadian Felix Auger-Aliassime and Americans Ben Shelton and Taylor Fritz at the ATP 500 indoor hardcourt event, which runs from October 26-November 1.

item.title: White House press secretary Zacharia fired in less than a week after facing criticism
item.description: The move comes after Trump said he had told her to reconsider the job following public scrutiny. Trump had described Zacharia as an attorney when he announced her appointment. During a Fox News interview, Zacharia said she did not pass the bar.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose, Trevor Hunnicutt, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: White House press secretary [USN:FWN45V14O TEXT:"Katie Zacharia"] was fired after less than a week on the job, two US officials said on Friday, after a rocky start as President Donald Trump 's top spokesperson. Zacharia was "let go" and is "transitioning out" of the press secretary position, according to two separate White House officials. She faced days of questions about her [USN:L6N4601D0 TEXT:"legal credentials"] and criticism of her performance in a news briefing and interviews. The departure leaves Trump without a key public messenger just over two weeks before November's midterm elections , a critical period when the president is seeking to tout his administration's accomplishments and help his fellow Republicans retain control of Congress. Trump told reporters earlier on Friday that he had asked Zacharia to reconsider whether to continue in her role after facing tough press coverage during her first days on the job. "I told her: 'I think you're better off being happy, and I'm not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.' There's nothing easy about this stuff," Trump told reporters as he departed the White House for a weekend trip. He added: "I said to her honestly, 'If I were you, I'd reconsider... think about it. But I would reconsider.'" Trump said he intended to revisit the conversation with Zacharia later. Zacharia started on Monday and held her debut White House briefing on Tuesday. She said she received a call about the press secretary role on October 7 and was offered the job to succeed [USN:FWN4491F6 TEXT:"Karoline Leavitt"] a week ago. She soon faced questions about her career, which she said included a tenure practicing law. Trump had also described her as an attorney. "I practiced international transaction law, with all the appropriate credentials," Zacharia said in an emailed statement on Wednesday. Reuters could not find records showing the Pepperdine University law school graduate was registered as an attorney or member of the bar in any US state or the District of Columbia. During a Fox News interview on Thursday, Zacharia said she [USN:L1N46201S TEXT:"did not pass the bar"] exam. Law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar. Zacharia and the White House did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment about her firing. Earlier on Friday, she told reporters at the White House that she was looking forward to working with the press. Trump hired Zacharia after expressing concerns about the media coverage of his administration, feeling he needed a new spokesperson who could amplify his achievements, according to two people familiar with the conversations. In a phone interview with Fox on Friday, Trump said he was in no rush to name a new press secretary. Zacharia's quick exit meant she had what is believed to be the shortest tenure of any press secretary in the role's history. "Records are made to be broken," Anthony Scaramucci, who served as director of communications for 10 days during Trump's first administration, said on X. "But I take no pleasure in other people's pain."

item.title: Sheinbaum y Bukele no discutieron públicamente sobre sus sistemas educativos
item.description: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, y el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, no discutieron públicamente sobre sus sistemas educativos, contrario a lo que sugieren publicaciones con un video alterado de la mandataria mexicana y un discurso de su homólogo salvadoreño en el que no menciona a México.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, y el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, no discutieron públicamente sobre sus sistemas educativos, contrario a lo que sugieren publicaciones con un video alterado de la mandataria mexicana y un discurso de su homólogo salvadoreño en el que no menciona a México. Ejemplos en internet dicen que, después de que Bukele anunció en agosto la entrega de 50 mil becas, Sheinbaum declaró en una conferencia que él solo busca un "espectáculo". Según las publicaciones, el presidente salvadoreño le respondió en un evento. Sin embargo, no hay evidencia de que la presidenta hiciera el comentario que se le atribuye. Las imágenes del primer fragmento corresponden a una conferencia de prensa matutina del 24 de agosto y, de acuerdo con el video completo y la versión estenográfica , no hizo referencia a Bukele o a sus iniciativas. No se identificaron declaraciones similares de Sheinbaum en medios de comunicación y en sus cuentas de redes sociales oficiales . El equipo de Comunicación Social de Presidencia de México dijo a Reuters el 13 de octubre en un mensaje de WhatsApp que el contenido es falso. El presidente salvadoreño publicó el segundo fragmento del video en su canal de YouTube el 15 de septiembre. En él, pidió a la ministra de Educación avanzar en mejoras educativas y habló sobre las becas para estudios superiores, no hizo referencia al modelo educativo mexicano o Sheinbaum. La presidencia de El Salvador no respondió inmediatamente a una solicitud de comentarios. Reuters ha abordado otras publicaciones que adjudican comentarios sin sustento a los políticos. VEREDICTO Falso. La presidenta de México, Claudia Sheinbaum, no criticó el programa de becas de Nayib Bukele y su homólogo salvadoreño no respondió a esos cuestionamientos. Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos. Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

item.title: Real Madrid pede saída do presidente da LaLiga após comparação com propaganda nazista
item.description: O Real Madrid pediu nesta sexta-feira a renúncia do presidente da LaLiga, Javier Tebas, depois que ele comparou a retórica da diretoria do clube aos métodos de propaganda utilizados pelo Partido Nazista na Alemanha.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Real Madrid pediu nesta sexta-feira a renúncia do presidente da LaLiga, Javier Tebas, depois que ele comparou a retórica da diretoria do clube aos métodos de propaganda utilizados pelo Partido Nazista na Alemanha. Tebas escreveu na manhã desta sexta-feira nas redes sociais que “a diretoria do Real Madrid conduz uma orquestra de porta-vozes e a Real Madrid TV lidera o coro”. O presidente da LaLiga estava respondendo a artigos de dois jornalistas que afirmavam que ele e a LaLiga estavam agindo contra os interesses do Real. Tebas acrescentou que os autores no jornal El Debate estavam amplificando uma mensagem em nome da diretoria do Real Madrid. A Reuters solicitou um comentário ao El Debate. A demanda do Real Madrid para que Tebas saia imediatamente aprofunda a disputa entre o clube e o presidente da LaLiga. Em setembro, o Real pediu a nomeação de um novo presidente da LaLiga em resposta a Tebas, que classificou as reclamações do clube sobre as decisões de arbitragem como “uma cortina de fumaça” para encobrir suas deficiências em campo. Tebas criticou, na sexta-feira, a cobertura da Real Madrid TV sobre a arbitragem em suas partidas. “O roteiro deles é sempre o mesmo: selecionar as jogadas que lhes convêm, repetir as queixas, alimentar a desconfiança e apontar o dedo para os inimigos”, escreveu ele. “Esse método lembra os mecanismos de propaganda usados por Goebbels, ministro da Propaganda da Alemanha nazista." “A comparação é com essas técnicas de propaganda, não com uma ideologia ou, é claro, com a torcida madridista”, acrescentou o presidente da LaLiga. O Real Madrid divulgou um comunicado na sexta-feira pedindo que Tebas renuncie aos cargos de presidente da LaLiga e vice-presidente da Real Federação Espanhola de Futebol. O comunicado considerou “intolerável e extraordinariamente grave” o fato de Tebas ter usado “uma comparação com os métodos de propaganda do regime nazista para desacreditar nosso clube, sua diretoria e sua emissora de TV”. “A conduta repetida de Tebas demonstra falta de neutralidade, respeito e imparcialidade, incompatível com suas responsabilidades institucionais”, afirmou o Real. “É inaceitável que ele se aproveite até mesmo de perguntas, informações ou opiniões de jornalistas não ligados ao clube para direcionar suas acusações contra nós, atribuindo-nos ações de terceiros pelas quais não temos qualquer responsabilidade.” Tebas, de 64 anos, eleito pelos 42 clubes profissionais das duas principais divisões da Espanha, é presidente da LaLiga desde 2013. Em 2023, ele foi reeleito sem oposição até 2027.

item.title: Ações europeias fecham melhor semana desde junho com balanços amenizando impacto de vendas em tecnologia
item.description: As ações europeias subiram nesta sexta-feira, encerrando sua melhor semana desde o final de junho, com sólidos resultados financeiros ajudando a amenizar o impacto de uma onda global de vendas de ações do setor de tecnologia.
item.dc:creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: As ações europeias subiram nesta sexta-feira, encerrando sua melhor semana desde o final de junho, com sólidos resultados financeiros ajudando a amenizar o impacto de uma onda global de vendas de ações do setor de tecnologia. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) subiu 0,7%, para 644,74 pontos, atingindo a maior cotação em mais de três semanas. O índice de referência acumulou alta de mais de 2% na semana. “Esta semana demonstrou o valor da diversificação quando o mercado tecnológico concentrado dos EUA fica sob pressão”, disse Daniela Hathorn, analista sênior de mercado da Capital.com. Uma onda de vendas em ações de empresas de tecnologia de grande destaque, motivada por preocupações com a crescente dependência de dívida para desenvolver infraestrutura de IA, aliada a receios quanto à concorrência da China, prejudicou as ações do setor de tecnologia nesta semana. No entanto, resultados sólidos da fabricante de equipamentos para chips de computador ASML (ASML.AS) , da fornecedora de sistemas de chips Aixtron (AIXGn.DE) e da fabricante de equipamentos de telecomunicações Ericsson (ERICb.ST) ajudaram a melhorar o ânimo do mercado. “Uma temporada de resultados financeiros muito positiva vai realmente impulsionar o ânimo dos investidores. Isso pode levar os mercados de volta a alguns dos picos que vimos recentemente”, disse Michael Field, estrategista-chefe de ações da Morningstar. Espera-se que os lucros das empresas do STOXX 600 aumentem 20,7% no terceiro trimestre em relação ao ano anterior, uma ligeira queda em relação à previsão de crescimento de 21% divulgada na semana passada, segundo dados da LSEG I/B/E/S. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) fechou em alta de 0,67%, a 644,43 pontos. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) avançou 0,38%, a 10.881,90 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) subiu 0,94%, a 25.622,42 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) ganhou 0,28%, a 7.956,70 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve valorização de 0,93%, a 49.857,18 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou alta de 0,77%, a 19.326,30 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) valorizou-se 1,01%, a 9.468,47 pontos.

item.title: Thames Water wins majority support among key Class B creditors for recapitalisation
item.description: Thames Water said on Friday it had reached an agreement with key Class B creditors on a proposed recapitalisation, securing support from holders of more than 60% of its junior Class B debt and advancing efforts to restructure Britain's biggest water utility.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thames Water said on Friday it had reached an agreement with key Class B creditors on a proposed recapitalisation, securing support from holders of more than 60% of its junior Class B debt and advancing efforts to restructure Britain's biggest water utility. The proposal would see about £1 billion ($1.33 billion) of Class B debt written off, with those creditors receiving a roughly 5.9% recovery through equity and other rights in the restructured company in return. The deal marks progress for Thames Water's senior creditors, known as London & Valley Water consortium, who are pursuing a rescue plan involving debt writedowns and fresh equity investment to avert temporary government control of the utility. L&VW declined to comment. The utility, weighed down by about £20 billion in debt, is seeking to overhaul its debt-laden balance sheet through a broader recapitalisation as it works to improve its finances and services amid mounting fines for polluting rivers with sewage. On Thursday, Thames Water [USN:L8N4611UT TEXT:"said"] it needed to increase its emergency funding facility by £2.4 billion to £5.4 billion to avoid running out of cash before its planned recapitalisation is completed. Thames Water said talks with L&VW and regulators on the proposed recapitalisation were ongoing, with no decision yet taken on whether to proceed with the consortium's rescue plan. The future of Thames Water is being closely watched after Prime Minister Andy Burnham last month [USN:L8N45L19H TEXT:"pledged"] legislation allowing public ownership of water companies while the government and regulators consider the L&VW rescue plan for the utility. ($1 = 0.7511 pounds)

item.title: 米当局、ＡＩ悪用の選挙妨害に警戒呼び掛け 11月の中間選挙控え
item.description: [ワシントン １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン １６日 ロイター] - 米連邦捜査局（ＦＢＩ）とサイバーセキュリティー・インフラセキュリティー庁（ＣＩＳＡ）は１６日、来月の中間選挙を控え、人工知能（ＡＩ）を悪用した手口に警戒するよう選挙関係者と国民に呼び掛けた。

ＦＢＩとＣＩＳＡの警告によると、ハッカーはパスワードやその他の機密データを盗み出すための偽のテキストメッセージや電子メールを用いて、中間選挙を妨害しようとする恐れがあるという。

警告では「選挙関係者や候補者、その政治組織は、悪意あるサイバー犯罪者にとって魅力的な標的となっている」と指摘した。

また、トランプ米大統領が変更を主張するＡＩの呼称である「スーパーインテリジェンス」（超知能、ＳＩ）により、ハッカーは不正な電子メールやテキストメッセージをより説得力のあるものに見せかけるよう巧妙化させていると述べた。

item.title: Police seek answers after children killed in Oregon school shooting
item.description: US police were investigating on Friday why a 16-year-old boy shot dead three children and a teacher at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, and how he got hold of the long gun used in his attack.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US police were investigating on Friday why a 16-year-old boy shot dead three children and a teacher at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, and how he got hold of the long gun used in his attack. The latest deadly school shooting in the United States [USN:L1N461173 TEXT:"unfolded on Thursday afternoon"] when the teenager, who has not been publicly identified, shot through a locked door at Silver Rail Elementary School in central Oregon, according to the Bend Police Department. The teenager killed three children aged 5, 8 and 11 and one teacher before he himself was shot dead by an armed bystander who had pursued him into the school, Police Chief Mike Krantz said at a Thursday evening press conference. Such shootings have become common in the US, with each one reviving debates over gun laws in a country where a right to "keep and bear Arms" is protected under the Constitution's Second Amendment. BYSTANDER INTERVENED The bystander has not been publicly identified by police, although the New York Times reported that he was the father of two young girls who attend the school. Oregon Governor Tina Kotek said at the press conference that the bystander "heroically intervened to stop further loss of life." Beyond those killed, a 7-year-old student and a 54-year-old teacher were taken to hospital with critical injuries. It was not clear if the shooter had any prior connection to the school, which has about 450 students from kindergarten through the fifth grade, roughly ages 5 to 11, and 40 staff members. The New York Times and other outlets, citing unnamed law enforcement officials, identified the teenager as John J. Griffin II, and investigators searched his home and seized electronic devices. They believe he used a 12-gauge pump-action Maverick 88 shotgun in the attack, which police say is registered to his mother, the Times reported. Officials at the Bend Police Department, who did not respond to questions on Friday, were due to give updates on their investigation at an afternoon press conference. GUN LAW DEBATES Some of the deadliest school attacks in the US include those at Columbine High School in 1999, Sandy Hook Elementary School in 2012, Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in 2018 and Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas, in 2022. Advocates for gun-owners' rights have argued for arming teachers as a means of defense. The Gun Owners of America advocacy group pointed to the armed bystander's intervention in Bend as evidence for their position. Residents of the small city of Bend were left grieving after the attack, which unfolded in minutes, with emergency responders receiving a call at 12:59 p.m. PDT (1959 GMT) from a person in a vehicle who reported being shot at multiple times by someone with a long gun, police said. In the minutes afterwards, dozens of calls were received saying the shooter had entered the school. Officers arrived at 1:02 p.m. and moments later an officer reported the shooter had been killed, police said. Officers entered and confirmed the teenager was dead.

item.title: Stars sign David Perron, 38, to one-year contract
item.description: The Dallas Stars signed forward David Perron to a one-year, $850,000 contract on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Dallas Stars signed forward David Perron to a one-year, $850,000 contract on Friday. Perron, 38, will be playing in his 20th NHL season with his eighth team. He totaled 28 points (13 goals, 15 assists) in 65 games last season split with the Ottawa Senators and Detroit Red Wings. "We are excited to welcome David and his family to the Stars organization," general manager Jim Nill said. "He brings a competitive mindset and a proven ability to perform in big moments. We believe his veteran leadership and skill set will be a valuable addition to our group as we continue to build toward our goal of winning a Stanley Cup." A Stanley Cup champion with the St. Louis Blues, Perron has totaled 812 points (332 goals, 480 assists) in 1,239 career games with the Blues, Edmonton Oilers, Pittsburgh Penguins, Anaheim Ducks, Vegas Golden Knights, Red Wings and Senators. He was selected by St. Louis with the 26th overall pick of the 2007 NHL Draft. --Field Level Media

Oct 16 : CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator and entities linked to him have sold nearly $1 billion of stock, mostly under prearranged trading plans, since the AI cloud company's IPO in March last year, according to regulatory filings. The sales began about two months after the stock hit a record high in June 2025. The shares have tumbled since and were on track to lose about 24 per cent this week as investors worried about the Nvidia-backed company's heavy capital spending and the debt needed to fund it amid rising bets on interest-rate hikes. CoreWeave did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Here are some more details:

• The sales totaled more than 10 million shares, according to the filings. As of Thursday's close, CoreWeave had a valuation of $38.44 billion. • The sales were made by Intrator and affiliated entities such as Omnadora Capital, where Intrator serves as managing member, and two trusts. • Most of these sales, excluding roughly $40 million, were made under prearranged trading plans that allow executives to sell shares on a preset schedule, and do not necessarily reflect management's view of the business. • The roughly $40 million that was not part of prearranged plans was sell-to-cover sales, where shares were sold on the market to pay taxes on vested stock. • The selling occurred as CoreWeave rapidly expanded its data-center footprint and increased spending on Nvidia chips to meet demand for AI computing, while building a revenue backlog of more than $129 billion. • In August, the company raised its annual capital expenditure forecast to be between $35 billion and $39 billion.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 米ロ軽油合意、なし崩し的に制裁緩和の恐れ＝ゼレンスキー氏
item.description:
Yuliia Dysa
［キーウ １６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Yuliia Dysa

［キーウ　１６日　ロイター］ - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は１６日、トランプ米大統領がロシアと結んだ軽油供給合意について、戦争を終わらせる意思を示さない侵略国に対する一段の制裁緩和に道を開くことになり、世界的なリスクにつながると警告した。

イラン戦争による燃料価格高騰の責任を、ロシアの製油所に対するウクライナ軍の攻撃に転嫁しようとするトランプ氏の姿勢も非難した。

ゼレンスキー氏は欧州連合（ＥＵ）首脳会議出席のため訪問中のブリュッセルで記者団に対し、「こうした軽油取引や合意は受け入れられない。次はガス取引、ガスの後には他の分野でも制裁が解除されるだろう。いずれ銀行システムや個人、化学産業にまで及ぶことになる」と厳しい認識を示した。

トランプ米大統領は９日、ロシアのプーチン大統領と電話会談を行い、ロシアが米国と世界市場にディーゼル（軽油）を供給することで合意したと発表した。nL6N45V0Z6

ロシアが２０２２年にウクライナへの全面侵攻を開始して以来、ロシア産化石燃料には段階的に制裁が科されてきた。ウクライナ政府は同盟国に対し、こうした供給への依存を終わらせるよう繰り返し求めている。

item.title: Trump move to restart direct US flights with Lebanon hits roadblock
item.description: The United Nations aviation agency has found Lebanon's main airport lacks valid certification, according to a report summary seen by Reuters, in a setback to US President Donald Trump's move to revive direct US-Beirut flights.
item.dc:creator: Allison Lampert, David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: The United Nations aviation agency has found Lebanon's main airport lacks valid certification, according to a report summary seen by Reuters, in a setback to US President Donald Trump's move to revive direct US-Beirut flights. Trump made the announcement in July and signed an order last month for [USN:FWN43N0RD TEXT:"the US government"] to allow direct flights from the US to Lebanon, reversing a four-decade-long suspension after TWA Flight 847 was hijacked and forced to land in Beirut in 1985. While the US Federal Aviation Administration and the Transportation Security Administration would still need to conduct safety reviews before flights could resume, the Lebanese embassy in Washington called Trump's order "a significant first step toward restoring direct air service between Lebanon and the United States." However, the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) technical assistance mission to Lebanon in July identified shortcomings at Beirut-Rafic Hariri International Airport and in the aviation system. The findings, which two senior industry officials familiar with the matter expect to delay the resumption of service, complicate efforts to follow up on an order Trump signed after meeting Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. Washington has backed Aoun as it pushes for Iran-backed Hezbollah to be disarmed. The agency sent its internal report, made at the request of the Lebanese Civil Aviation Authority (LCAA), to Lebanon in September. AIRPORT LACKS EMERGENCY PLAN: ICAO Beirut airport's firefighting resources are equipped for single-aisle planes, but not twin-aisle jetliners used for long-haul flights, according to a summary of ICAO's report. The airport also lacks an emergency plan, and its conditional certification has expired, the report said. "This is a serious and time-critical matter that must be addressed immediately to preserve the airport's operational status," the summary said. The report also found the Lebanese regulator LCAA lacks qualified inspectors to oversee air traffic control licensing, and has no fully established, operational and independent aircraft accident investigation authority with clearly defined roles. Such concerns were flagged during a two-day workshop last month where officials from ICAO, Lebanon's government, the FAA and others discussed efforts to revive direct air service, according to the industry officials and an agenda of the meeting seen by Reuters. Lebanon's Minister of Public Works and Transport Fayez Rasamny said Lebanon was taking steps to address the concerns, with efforts to certify the airport starting on Saturday. The LCAA expects to issue conditional certification in the coming days. "Most of the issues highlighted in the report had already been identified by the LCAA, and corrective action had already been initiated," Rasamny said in a statement, adding that progress had been delayed by war. Israeli forces remain in southern Lebanon and have continued strikes despite a US-brokered framework agreement signed in June between Israel and Lebanon. Hezbollah, which was not party to the deal, has rejected it. The FAA declined to comment. ICAO said it cannot comment on matters concerning specific countries, but said it conducts targeted analyses for member states. The US State Department advises Americans not to travel to Lebanon given safety concerns. It said the FAA advises caution for flights operating in Lebanese airspace due to heightened military activity in or around Syria, including the risks of errant long-range surface-to-air missiles originating from Syrian territory. MIDDLE EAST UNREST DISRUPTS AIR TRAVEL Foreign airlines have avoided large swathes of Middle East airspace because of missile and drone threats since US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February triggered regional hostilities, with an [USN:L6N4600LI TEXT:"airport"] in Saudi Arabia the latest site to come under attack. Lebanon and its national carrier have been praised domestically for maintaining air navigation services and flights, helping to prop up an economy that depends on tourism and remittances. Three US airline officials told Reuters on the condition of anonymity they do not think any American carriers would resume flights to Lebanon in the near term, citing security concerns. While there are no direct flights between Beirut and the United States, such service exists between Lebanon and some large European cities. The European Union Aviation Safety Agency said it was aware of the ICAO report and added that EU airlines must conduct their own assessment of an airport's safety and operational readiness before launching services.

Oct 16 : Wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant was named in India's squad for next month's two-test series in New Zealand on Friday, subject to fitness clearance, while pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah returned to the side. The Shubman Gill-led test squad featured few surprises, with selectors retaining the core of the team, including all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja and opener Yashasvi Jaiswal. Pant was recently ruled out of the first two India A test matches against New Zealand with a left side strain but was included in the senior squad pending medical clearance. India begin the two-match test series in Wellington on November 19 before the second and final match in Christchurch from November 27.

item.title: ロシア、ウクライナ領内に「安保地帯」設置へ 交渉対象外＝プーチン氏
item.description: [モスクワ １６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ １６日 ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は１６日、ウクライナとの国境沿いのウクライナ領内で「安全保障地帯」の設置を進めていると明らかにし、将来的にウクライナと交渉が行われた場合でも、この安全保障地帯は交渉の対象にしないと述べた。

プーチン氏はこの日、軍服姿でロシア軍統合部隊の指揮所を視察。安全保障地帯の設置は２０２４─２５年にウクライナ軍がロシア西部クルスク州に侵攻したことへの対応になると説明し、「ロシア軍には、ロシア領から敵を排除する任務に加え、隣接地域に安全保障地帯を設ける任務も与えられている。この任務は成功裏に遂行されている」と述べた。

その上で、安全保障地帯の設置は「将来にわたりロシアの国境地域の絶対的な安全を確保すること」が目的だとし、これをウクライナとの和平交渉の議題にする考えはないと語った。

また、ロシア軍はウクライナ東部ドネツク州の制圧を進めているものの、同州の約１０％をまだ掌握できていないとも述べた。

ロシア大統領府のペスコフ報道官によると、計画されている安全保障地帯の総延長は６６０キロ。このうち約７０％はロシアがすでに支配下に置いているとしている。

プーチン氏の発言はテレビ中継された。

The Vatican said earlier on Friday that Leo had urged Putin to agree to a truce to allow the entry of first aid and food supplies into the town and to permit a voluntary evacuation of the civilian population.
